name: Eternal

headline.text: Q2 FY27: revenue ₹24,138 cr (+77.6% YoY), PAT ₹125 cr (+92.3% YoY).
Trailing twelve months: revenue ₹77,956 cr, EBITDA ₹2,200 cr (2.8% margin), PAT ₹493 cr.

claims.text: Revenue compounded at 93.7% a year over FY21–FY26 (₹1,994 cr → ₹54,364 cr).

citations.excerpt: Consolidated revenue from operations grew 169% … YoY to INR 54,364 crore in FY26 from INR 20,243 crore

claims.text: FY26 revenue growth of 168.6% was the fastest in 5 years.

citations.excerpt: Consolidated revenue from operations grew 169% … YoY to INR 54,364 crore in FY26 from INR 20,243 crore

claims.text: EBITDA margin expanded by 1933 bps over FY23–FY26 (−17.1% → 2.2%).
Debt-to-equity was 0.18 at FY27 end (0.04 at FY24).
Borrowings rose 7.7× from ₹749 cr to ₹5,757 cr over FY24–FY27.
Free cash flow (as computed by screener.in) was positive in 1 of the last 5 years, −₹2,988 cr in total.
Capex over the last 5 years was ₹3,037 cr, 6198% of operating cash flow (derived as operating cash flow − free cash flow).
Cash conversion cycle lengthened from -132 to 2 days over FY23–FY26.
Return on capital employed was 2% in FY26 (-6% in FY23).

statements.speaker: Gaurav Malhotra
statements.quote: Firstly, you seem to have raised the long-term guidance in quick commerce from 5-6% to 6%.

statements.speaker: Akshant Goyal
statements.quote: It's also a function of increase in average store sizes, etc. All these investments are clearly lining up in a way where we now have higher visibility on margins and we think at this point we're likely to end at the higher end of the range that we had guided earlier and hence, the communication.

statements.speaker: Swapnil Potdukhe
statements.quote: You mentioned last quarter that there will be some bit of seasonality in the Blinkit business, and that will help you grow meaningfully faster and you did deliver 21% QoQ volume growth.

statements.speaker: Swapnil Potdukhe
statements.quote: The other question is with respect to your capex guidance that you have said.

statements.speaker: Gaurav Malhotra
statements.quote: First question is on the overall EBITDA guidance or indication of $1 billion by FY29.

statements.speaker: Gaurav Malhotra
statements.quote: We do know about District EBITDA guidance of FY30.

statements.speaker: Akshant Goyal
statements.quote: We've given overall guidance of 60% CAGR and that would obviously mean some reasonable store expansion, but we're not planning to give out any specific number guidance on that.

statements.speaker: Akshant Goyal
statements.quote: Yes, it will not be 100%, but we are not guiding to a specific number.

statements.speaker: Akshant Goyal
statements.quote: We've tried to give you the building blocks of what the 60% CAGR guidance is based upon.

statements.speaker: Manish Adukia
statements.quote: Where I was coming from was also the building blocks in terms of, and I know you don't want to give like a three-year store guidance, but if you were to think about user growth versus frequency versus average order value, if you can maybe give us a pecking order of what drives the most amount of growth versus followed by the second, followed by the third, that would also be helpful.

statements.speaker: Akshant Goyal
statements.quote: I'm not saying that this metric will not go up, but I'm saying that the reason we're not providing a guidance for this metric and instead we're giving guidance for the overall growth of the business is because these variables and the building blocks of how we look at the business might evolve as we go along.

statements.speaker: Vijit Jain
statements.quote: Any sort of guidance you can give on how you're thinking about capex beyond the store additions that you would do.

statements.speaker: Akshant Goyal
statements.quote: We're not giving specific guidance but increasingly, as we also mentioned in the letter, a large part of our growth will come from geographic diversification so we will see that mix change over time.

statements.speaker: Manish Adukia
statements.quote: I just wanted to tie up that guidance that you're saying that if competition is not irrational, it's only then you'll open 3,500 to 4,000 stores and only then you'll achieve 100% YoY growth.

statements.speaker: Manish Adukia
statements.quote: You've maintained your $3 billion NOV guidance for going-out in FY30, which would imply north of 30% CAGR over the next four years.

statements.speaker: Akshant Goyal
statements.quote: Even though we might see capex per store going up over the next few quarters, we don't expect net working capital to be beyond those 18 days that we had shared earlier, so that should remain within range and hence, as a consequence of that, the ROCE outcome should still be north of 40%.

statements.speaker: Akshant Goyal
statements.quote: As we have mentioned in question 11, the new labor codes do not impact our long-term margin guidance.

statements.speaker: Akshant Goyal
statements.quote: As of now, as we have mentioned, we expect year-on-year growth to continue slowly trending up towards 20% YoY, is what our current sense on the market is.
